sections.subtitleText: The upsides first: cheap and convenient. Very easy to use as a quick meal component. Still keeps some fibre. The fibre keeps it more useful than a plain sugary sauce-style bean product. Has practical comfort-food appeal. People actually eat it, which matters in the real world.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: The drawbacks next: added sugar is a major category problem. Legumes are supposed to win on slow-carb behaviour, and this pushes the opposite way. Processing drags the category fit down. The canned sweet-sauce format makes it a worse version of what legumes are supposed to be. Weak protein usefulness for a legume. It does not deliver the strong fibre-plus-protein combo that defines elite legumes.
